question: What happens right after a tribunal finds a midwife guilty of gross professional misconduct?

options.A: The midwife is automatically promoted to a senior administrative rank
options.B: The affected patient is appointed as the new head of the nursing unit
options.C: Appropriate sanctions are applied, such as suspension or removal from the register
options.D: The case is permanently closed without any record kept in the registry

explanation: Guilty verdicts lead to professional penalties, which can include suspension or removing the practitioner's name from the official register. [learn more](BMP127_U3_T4#BMP127_U3_T4_h5)

question: Why is writing down care notes right away so important in midwifery?

options.A: It is required primarily for hospital statistical billing purposes
options.B: It allows doctors to bypass writing their own clinical notes
options.C: It guarantees that the hospital will never be sued by patients
options.D: It serves as primary legal evidence of the care provided to the patient

explanation: Accurate, written records are treated by courts as the most reliable proof of what happened during care. [learn more](BMP127_U3_T4#BMP127_U3_T4_h6)

question: A midwife forgets to record a medication dose and squeezes the entry into a past date. What is the legal meaning of this?

options.A: It is standard administrative practice as long as the drug was given
options.B: It constitutes falsification of records, which worsens legal liability
options.C: It is acceptable provided the head of department countersigns it
options.D: It is a minor clerical error with no professional consequences

explanation: Backdating or altering records after an incident destroys credibility and is treated as serious fraud during investigations. [learn more](BMP127_U3_T4#BMP127_U3_T4_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of professional indemnity insurance for a practicing midwife?

options.A: Providing financial protection and legal defense support in civil lawsuits
options.B: Replacing the need to register annually with the regulatory council
options.C: Covering the cost of personal medical treatment during illness
options.D: Guaranteeing automatic promotion and salary increments every year

explanation: Indemnity insurance protects midwives against the high costs of legal defense and damages if a patient sues. [learn more](BMP127_U3_T4#BMP127_U3_T4_h7)

question: Which proactive practice helps a midwife avoid professional misconduct or negligence claims?

options.A: Avoiding documentation to prevent patients from reading their charts
options.B: Delegating all complex deliveries entirely to untrained assistants
options.C: Refusing to communicate with patient relatives during emergencies
options.D: Practicing strictly within evidence-based guidelines and established scope

explanation: Following approved protocols and staying within your trained scope ensures safe care and prevents legal trouble. [learn more](BMP127_U3_T4#BMP127_U3_T4_h7)

question: What is the main focus of modern maternal and child health care in Nigeria?

options.A: Focusing solely on major tertiary surgeries
options.B: Moving toward prevention and grassroots care
options.C: Relying entirely on foreign medical aid
options.D: Eliminating the need for community midwives

explanation: Modern healthcare trends place greater emphasis on stopping complications before they start by bringing services closer to local communities. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T1#BMP217_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why do contemporary Nigerian midwives need to understand new healthcare innovations?

options.A: Traditional clinical methods are completely banned in hospitals
options.B: Technology has fully replaced the need for human clinical judgment
options.C: Midwives actively shape policies and test new lifesaving service models
options.D: Midwives are required to manufacture their own medical equipment

explanation: Because midwives drive frontline care, they must adapt to and guide the new tools and delivery models transforming the profession. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T1#BMP217_U1_T1_h1)

question: What does the term mHealth mean in midwifery practice?

options.A: Using mobile phones and wireless technology for health services
options.B: Storing physical patient case notes in a metal filing cabinet
options.C: Operating heavy diagnostic machinery using battery power
options.D: Transporting mothers to the hospital via ambulance bikes

explanation: mHealth stands for mobile health, which leverages phones and handheld devices to improve health delivery and communication. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T1#BMP217_U1_T1_h2)

question: A pregnant woman in a remote village frequently misses her antenatal visits due to forgetfulness. Which mHealth tool can best help solve this?

options.A: An electronic surgical database stored at the national headquarters
options.B: A mobile app designed exclusively for tertiary hospital doctors
options.C: Automated SMS appointment reminders sent directly to her phone
options.D: A high-frequency radio broadcast regarding obstetric surgery

explanation: Automated text message reminders are a proven, low-cost mHealth strategy for prompting patients to attend scheduled clinic visits. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T1#BMP217_U1_T1_h2)

question: What is the main benefit of point-of-care diagnostic tools in rural clinics?

options.A: They are used exclusively for major surgical operations
options.B: They provide rapid test results directly at the patient's bedside
options.C: They eliminate the need for any trained clinical personnel
options.D: They require expensive mainframe computers to function properly

explanation: Point-of-care tests give immediate answers, allowing midwives to start urgent treatment without waiting for centralized laboratory processing. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T1#BMP217_U1_T1_h3)

question: How does the non-pneumatic anti-shock garment (NASG) help a woman suffering from severe bleeding after birth?

options.A: It delivers a direct intravenous transfusion of whole blood
options.B: It stimulates the uterine muscles to contract and stop the bleeding
options.C: It lowers the patient's body temperature to prevent infection
options.D: It applies external pressure to force blood flow back to vital organs

explanation: The NASG is a pressure wrap that stabilizes a bleeding woman by keeping blood circulating around the heart, lungs, and brain. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T1#BMP217_U1_T1_h3)

question: Who is the primary autonomous caregiver for normal, low-risk pregnancies in a midwife-led model?

options.A: The pediatric surgeon
options.B: The midwife
options.C: The consultant obstetrician
options.D: The hospital pharmacist

explanation: In midwife-led care, the midwife holds primary responsibility for managing normal pregnancies and uncomplicated childbirths. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T1#BMP217_U1_T1_h4)

question: Why is community involvement important when introducing new maternal health programs in rural areas?

options.A: Community members are required to fund all hospital construction projects
options.B: Government policies forbid doctors from working in rural villages
options.C: Local ownership and involvement ensure the population accepts and utilizes the services
options.D: Traditional leaders prefer to replace licensed midwives entirely

explanation: When communities help design and support health initiatives, cultural barriers drop and local women are more likely to seek care. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T1#BMP217_U1_T1_h4)

question: What does task shifting involve in healthcare delivery?

options.A: Delegating specific clinical duties to appropriately trained lower-cadre staff
options.B: Rotating midwifery students between different hospital wards
options.C: Transferring all hospitalized patients to distant tertiary facilities
options.D: Moving doctors away from clinics to administrative offices

explanation: Task shifting optimizes workforce distribution by training capable cadres to handle tasks usually reserved for higher-level professionals. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T1#BMP217_U1_T1_h5)

question: What is the main goal of including pregnant women in Universal Health Coverage (UHC) schemes?

options.A: To transfer healthcare funding control entirely to private pharmaceutical companies
options.B: To ensure that all births take place exclusively in private clinics
options.C: To eliminate the need for keeping medical records during antenatal visits
options.D: To prevent financial hardship and delays caused by out-of-pocket expenses

explanation: Financial barriers often force families to delay seeking care; UHC aims to make essential maternal services affordable and accessible to all. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T1#BMP217_U1_T1_h5)

question: Why do some health technology projects fail in rural primary health centers?

options.A: Government policies strictly forbid the use of electronic devices
options.B: Midwives refuse to use any form of modern medical equipment
options.C: They fail to account for local challenges like erratic power supply and lack of training
options.D: Patients prefer complex surgical procedures over simple diagnostics

explanation: Without reliable electricity, maintenance, and proper staff training, even the best technological innovations quickly become abandoned. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T1#BMP217_U1_T1_h6)

question: A rural clinic receives new digital tablets for recording antenatal data, but the midwives struggle to use them and the internet is unstable. What should be done FIRST?

options.A: Wait for the patients to bring their own mobile internet routers to the clinic
options.B: Provide practical staff training and establish reliable offline backup solutions with solar power
options.C: Transfer all the midwives to a teaching hospital in the state capital
options.D: Throw away the tablets and return entirely to paper registers forever

explanation: Addressing the root operational problems through training and power support ensures that digital tools can be used effectively despite local constraints. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T1#BMP217_U1_T1_h6)

question: What is the key feature of a midwife-led continuity of care model?

options.A: A pregnant woman is assigned a different doctor for every antenatal clinic visit.
options.B: Midwives only manage women during the actual delivery room stage of labor.
options.C: Care is provided exclusively inside major tertiary teaching hospitals by obstetricians.
options.D: A woman is cared for by a small, familiar group of midwives throughout her pregnancy and birth.

explanation: Continuity models center on the same known midwife or small team following the woman across the entire childbearing journey. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T2#BMP217_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why does seeing a familiar midwife during pregnancy and birth help a woman?

options.A: It guarantees that the woman will never experience any medical complications.
options.B: It allows the midwife to perform surgical procedures without consulting doctors.
options.C: It builds a trusting relationship that helps reduce anxiety and improve communication.
options.D: It completely removes the need for any laboratory investigations or scans.

explanation: Knowing the healthcare provider makes women more comfortable sharing worries and asking questions, which supports better health outcomes. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T2#BMP217_U1_T2_h1)

question: Which statement describes woman-centred care in midwifery?

options.A: Prioritizing the personal choices, values, and autonomy of the woman.
options.B: Ensuring every labor follows the exact same standardized timeline.
options.C: Leaving all health decisions entirely up to the senior medical consultant.
options.D: Following hospital administrative routines above the wishes of the patient.

explanation: Woman-centred care respects the individual needs, preferences, and cultural background of each mother. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T2#BMP217_U1_T2_h2)

question: What does safeguarding normality mean during continuous midwifery support?

options.A: Treating pregnancy as a high-risk medical disease from the very first visit.
options.B: Forcing every woman to have a completely unmedicated home birth.
options.C: Refusing to transfer any patient to a doctor under any circumstance.
options.D: Minimizing unnecessary medical interventions while keeping watch for danger signs.

explanation: Midwives support normal physiological birth by avoiding routine interventions that are not medically required, while remaining ready to act if complications arise. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T2#BMP217_U1_T2_h2)

question: How does caseload midwifery differ from team midwifery?

options.A: Caseload midwifery assigns one primary midwife with a partner, whereas team midwifery uses a larger shared group.
options.B: Team midwifery involves a single midwife caring for hundreds of women alone.
options.C: Caseload midwifery does not include postnatal visits after the baby is born.
options.D: Caseload midwifery is only practiced inside operating theatres by obstetric surgeons.

explanation: Caseload models focus on one primary caregiver relationship, while team models distribute women across a slightly larger pool of known midwives. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T2#BMP217_U1_T2_h3)

question: A pregnant woman wants a midwife-led model where she is almost guaranteed to have her primary named midwife present at her birth. Which model should she choose?

options.A: General hospital outpatient clinic
options.B: Caseload midwifery
options.C: Random doctor rotation scheme
options.D: Emergency obstetric surgical unit

explanation: Caseload midwifery offers the highest chance of continuity because one primary midwife commits to being on call for that specific woman. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T2#BMP217_U1_T2_h3)

question: What do research reviews show about the impact of midwife-led continuity models on epidural use?

options.A: Women using these models are less likely to require regional analgesia like epidurals.
options.B: Women in these models are forced to use epidurals during every single birth.
options.C: Epidural rates remain exactly the same regardless of who provides the care.
options.D: Midwife-led care increases the need for continuous general anesthesia.

explanation: Continuous support from a known midwife helps women cope with labor pain naturally, reducing the need for regional pain relief. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T2#BMP217_U1_T2_h4)

question: Why are effective referral pathways important alongside midwife-led units?

options.A: To make sure all normal births are automatically transferred to surgical theatres.
options.B: To ensure women who develop unexpected complications can get prompt medical help from doctors.
options.C: To replace antenatal education with administrative paperwork.
options.D: To prevent midwives from ever having to touch a pregnant woman in labor.

explanation: While midwife-led care is excellent for normal pregnancies, safety depends on swift escalation and transfer when obstetric or medical intervention is required. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T2#BMP217_U1_T2_h4)

question: Which level of the Nigerian healthcare system is the first grassroots point for community maternity care?

options.A: Federal ministry health headquarters
options.B: Primary health care centres
options.C: National tertiary teaching hospitals
options.D: Private specialist surgical clinics

explanation: Primary health care centres are located closest to communities and serve as the first point of contact for routine maternal and child health services. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T2#BMP217_U1_T2_h5)

question: How can midwives in Nigeria work effectively alongside Traditional Birth Attendants (TBAs)?

options.A: By allowing TBAs to perform caesarean sections inside primary health clinics.
options.B: By taking over TBA herbal shops and running them as maternity pharmacies.
options.C: By ignoring them completely and relying only on federal government memos.
options.D: By engaging them to encourage women to seek skilled attendance at health facilities.

explanation: Collaborating with local community figures like TBAs helps redirect women toward safe, facility-based skilled birth attendants. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T2#BMP217_U1_T2_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common challenge when setting up midwife continuity models in resource-limited settings?

options.A: An overabundance of surplus midwives causing widespread staff underemployment
options.B: Shortages of qualified midwifery personnel leading to severe workplace burnout
options.C: Financial constraints linked to high out-of-pocket payments for health services
options.D: Infrastructure gaps including frequent power outages and bad roads

explanation: Staff shortages, not surpluses, represent a major barrier to rolling out sustainable midwifery continuity programs in resource-limited regions. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T2#BMP217_U1_T2_h6)

question: A primary health clinic suffers from staff shortages, causing midwives to experience severe burnout from 24-hour on-call duties. What is a practical administrative solution?

options.A: Closing the maternity unit permanently and stopping all antenatal care
options.B: Implementing flexible shift-sharing rosters and team rotation schedules
options.C: Abolishing the use of clinical records to save time during working hours
options.D: Forcing remaining midwives to work double shifts without any backup

explanation: Organizing shared team rotas helps distribute the on-call burden fairly, protecting individual midwives from extreme exhaustion. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T2#BMP217_U1_T2_h6)

question: What does professional autonomy mean for a practicing midwife?

options.A: Having the clinical and legal authority to make independent decisions within one's scope of practice.
options.B: Working completely isolated from doctors and refusing all hospital transfers.
options.C: Setting personal hospital fees and managing administrative budgets independently.
options.D: Being legally permitted to perform major general surgeries without any medical training.

explanation: Autonomy allows midwives to use their professional training to assess, plan, and provide care independently for normal pregnancies and births. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T2#BMP217_U1_T2_h7)

question: Why is building respect between midwives and obstetricians important for continuity care?

options.A: It stops doctors from ever visiting the maternity ward or seeing patients.
options.B: It eliminates the need for any clinical guidelines or professional standards.
options.C: It ensures smooth teamwork and safer patient transfers when complications occur.
options.D: It gives midwives complete administrative control over all hospital departments.

explanation: Healthy collaboration between midwives and doctors creates a safer system where women can move seamlessly between normal and specialized medical care. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T2#BMP217_U1_T2_h7)

question: What is the primary focus of Respectful Maternity Care in addition to preventing maternal mortality?

options.A: Speeding up the duration of the active first stage of labor
options.B: Ensuring every delivery is conducted via elective cesarean section
options.C: The emotional and psychological well-being of the mother
options.D: Reducing the overall cost of hospital delivery supplies

explanation: RMC ensures that care looks beyond just physical survival to care for the psychological and emotional needs of the birthing mother. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T3#BMP217_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why does Respectful Maternity Care encourage moving away from strict, medically driven care?

options.A: Doctors are no longer legally permitted to manage normal low-risk deliveries
options.B: Clinical care completely ignores the physical health of the newborn infant
options.C: Traditional birth attendants perform better than trained hospital midwives
options.D: Paternalistic medical attitudes often neglect the dignity and autonomy of women

explanation: Respectful Maternity Care challenges the old habit of making decisions for women without involving them or respecting their personal dignity. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T3#BMP217_U1_T3_h1)

question: Which of the following is included under the Universal Rights of Childbearing Women?

options.A: Right to choose the exact medical doctor on duty
options.B: Right to a private room for every antenatal visit
options.C: Right to absolute freedom from discrimination during care
options.D: Right to receive free baby formula at discharge

explanation: The charter guarantees that every woman receives fair treatment without discrimination based on status, tribe, or religion. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T3#BMP217_U1_T3_h2)

question: A midwife refuses to attend quickly to a young woman in labor because she cannot afford the required admission deposit. Which specific right is being violated?

options.A: Right to timely healthcare and freedom from extortion
options.B: Right to choose a preferred birth position
options.C: Right to exclusive postnatal bed space
options.D: Right to absolute medical confidentiality

explanation: Withholding or delaying emergency care due to financial demands violates a woman's right to timely care and protection from exploitation. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T3#BMP217_U1_T3_h2)

question: What does the term obstetric violence include in a healthcare facility setting?

options.A: Physical abuse, humiliation, and lack of informed consent
options.B: Unavoidable surgical scars following an emergency operation
options.C: Any complication arising strictly from a multiple birth
options.D: Normal physiological fatigue experienced after a long labor

explanation: Obstetric violence covers behaviors like verbal abuse, humiliation, physical mistreatment, and performing procedures without consent. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T3#BMP217_U1_T3_h3)

question: Why are practices like performing routine episiotomies without consent classified as disrespect or abuse?

options.A: They violate a woman's bodily autonomy and right to informed choices
options.B: They are completely banned by the World Health Organization worldwide
options.C: They always result in permanent infertility for the childbearing woman
options.D: They are only performed by junior nursing students without supervision

explanation: Performing medical procedures on a patient's body without their knowledge or consent strips them of their basic autonomy. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T3#BMP217_U1_T3_h3)

question: What practical tool serves as the expression of patient autonomy in a maternity ward?

options.A: The doctor's prescription sheet
options.B: The admission register
options.C: The hospital discharge summary
options.D: Informed consent

explanation: Informed consent allows the woman to exercise her autonomy by agreeing to or refusing procedures after understanding them. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T3#BMP217_U1_T3_h4)

question: How does the principle of equity apply to everyday midwifery care in Nigeria?

options.A: Wealthy patients should be attended to before emergency cases
options.B: Government hospitals are exempt from practicing respectful maternity care
options.C: Every woman must receive the same high standard of respectful care regardless of status
options.D: Midwives only need to be polite to women who pay hospital fees promptly

explanation: Equity means fair treatment for all, ensuring that poverty or social standing never determines the quality of care a woman receives. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T3#BMP217_U1_T3_h4)

question: What is a major community-level consequence of harsh or disrespectful treatment in maternity hospitals?

options.A: Traditional birth attendants close down their clinics permanently
options.B: An immediate increase in government funding for health centers
options.C: Pregnant women demand more surgical interventions from doctors
options.D: Women avoid facilities and choose home or unassisted births

explanation: Bad treatment drives women away from formal healthcare facilities, leading them to seek care elsewhere, often with tragic results. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T3#BMP217_U1_T3_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a clinical risk when women delay hospital care due to fear of abuse?

options.A: Eclamptic seizures resulting from unmonitored high blood pressure
options.B: Severe postpartum hemorrhage from prolonged obstructed labor
options.C: Immediate spontaneous resolution of high blood pressure
options.D: Uterine rupture due to delayed management of labor complications

explanation: Delayed care worsens conditions like hypertension and hemorrhage; it never resolves them spontaneously. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T3#BMP217_U1_T3_h5)

question: What is a practical way for a midwife to demonstrate Respectful Maternity Care during a vaginal examination?

options.A: Conducting the examination quickly without informing the anxious patient
options.B: Asking a junior student to perform the check without supervision
options.C: Insisting that the husband leaves the room before any assessment begins
options.D: Explaining the procedure and asking for permission before touching the woman

explanation: Seeking consent and explaining every step preserves the woman's dignity and bodily integrity during intimate exams. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T3#BMP217_U1_T3_h6)

question: A woman in the first stage of labor requests to walk around the ward and lean on her sister for support. What should the attending midwife do?

options.A: Disallow the sister from staying because visitors are banned in the labor room
options.B: Encourage her mobility and welcome the sister as a supportive birth companion
options.C: Insist she lies flat on the delivery bed immediately to monitor contractions
options.D: Scold her for moving around and demand she saves her energy for pushing

explanation: RMC supports freedom of movement during labor and values the presence of a chosen birth companion for comfort. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T3#BMP217_U1_T3_h6)

question: Why is improving hospital working conditions essential for achieving sustainable Respectful Maternity Care?

options.A: Exhausted and unsupported staff working without basic supplies struggle to provide compassionate care
options.B: Midwives cannot legally practice unless they receive a monthly hazard allowance
options.C: International donors refuse to fund hospitals that have old medical equipment
options.D: Hospital management only responds to complaints when clinics are running at a loss

explanation: Systemic stress, burnout, and lack of basic resources directly contribute to harsh treatment and poor care on the wards. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T3#BMP217_U1_T3_h7)

question: Which of the following actions represents effective midwifery advocacy for better maternity services?

options.A: Leading quality improvement efforts and demanding better working conditions from management
options.B: Ignoring unit shortages and pretending everything is fine to avoid conflict
options.C: Reporting struggling colleagues directly to the police without internal dialogue
options.D: Telling patients to buy all hospital consumables from private chemist shops

explanation: Effective advocacy involves active participation in system reforms, mentoring, and pushing for resource availability to improve care. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T3#BMP217_U1_T3_h7)

question: What does the Maternal Mortality Ratio measure?

options.A: Deaths per 1,000 women of childbearing age
options.B: Total deaths in a specific hospital ward
options.C: Deaths per 100,000 live births
options.D: Infant deaths compared to maternal deaths

explanation: The Maternal Mortality Ratio is calculated specifically using live births as the denominator to show the risk per pregnancy episode. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T4#BMP217_U1_T4_h1)

question: Why do midwives and researchers study near-miss maternal morbidity cases?

options.A: Patients who survive never experience long-term trauma
options.B: Hospital insurance requires tracking all minor injuries
options.C: Near-miss cases are much easier to legally document
options.D: Survivors share similar complications with women who died

explanation: Looking at women who survived severe emergencies gives healthcare teams valuable clues about how to save others facing identical crises. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T4#BMP217_U1_T4_h1)

question: Which factor directly contributes to the FIRST delay in the Three Delays Model?

options.A: Poor road networks linking villages to the city
options.B: Failure to recognize danger signs at home
options.C: A lack of surgical tools inside the operating theatre
options.D: A shortage of blood bags in the main blood bank

explanation: The first delay happens at the community and household level when family members hesitate or fail to realize a serious emergency is occurring. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T4#BMP217_U1_T4_h2)

question: A woman with severe bleeding waits three hours for a commercial bus because her village has no ambulance. Which delay does this represent?

options.A: Delay in community mobilization meetings
options.B: Delay in reaching a health facility
options.C: Delay in receiving proper hospital treatment
options.D: Delay in deciding to seek care

explanation: Struggling with transport and distance to get to a clinic falls squarely under the second delay of the model. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T4#BMP217_U1_T4_h2)

question: What is a primary clinical responsibility of a community-based midwife during antenatal visits?

options.A: Screening for conditions like high blood pressure and anemia
options.B: Managing national health policy budgets for maternal care
options.C: Performing complex major abdominal surgeries in village clinics
options.D: Manufacturing routine pharmaceutical antibiotics locally

explanation: Community midwives focus heavily on regular antenatal checkups to catch common, dangerous conditions early before they spiral out of control. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T4#BMP217_U1_T4_h3)

question: How do community midwives help reduce the First Delay in obstetric emergencies?

options.A: By manufacturing emergency blood transfusion kits in the village
options.B: By importing advanced surgical machinery for rural clinics
options.C: By paving roads that connect remote villages to tertiary hospitals
options.D: By educating families to spot danger signs and plan early for birth

explanation: When midwives teach communities what normal versus dangerous symptoms look like, families make the decision to seek help much faster. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T4#BMP217_U1_T4_h3)

question: Which medical service distinguishes a Comprehensive EmOC facility from a Basic EmOC facility?

options.A: Giving oral iron supplements during antenatal care
options.B: Conducting routine manual placental removal
options.C: Performing caesarean section surgeries
options.D: Administering standard oxytocin injections

explanation: Only Comprehensive EmOC (CEmOC) facilities are equipped and staffed to carry out blood transfusions and major surgeries like caesarean sections. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T4#BMP217_U1_T4_h4)

question: Why is relying solely on community-based primary prevention insufficient to eliminate maternal deaths?

options.A: Traditional birth attendants solve all surgical problems locally
options.B: Unpredictable life-threatening complications will still occur during childbirth
options.C: Midwives are legally prohibited from managing normal deliveries alone
options.D: Pregnant women in rural areas refuse to attend community health talks

explanation: Some severe obstetric emergencies, such as sudden hemorrhage or obstructed labor, happen without warning and require advanced facility-based surgery. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T4#BMP217_U1_T4_h4)

question: What is the primary goal of a Maternal Death Surveillance and Response (MDSR) system?

options.A: To investigate every maternal death and implement corrective local actions
options.B: To calculate exact tax rates for families living in rural communities
options.C: To restrict pregnant women from traveling far away from home
options.D: To punish healthcare workers who make clinical mistakes in surgery

explanation: MDSR is designed to track and learn from every loss of life so the health system can fix systemic flaws and prevent future tragedies. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T4#BMP217_U1_T4_h5)

question: What happens when a country has weak vital registration and poor civil recording systems?

options.A: Pregnant women completely stop visiting modern health facilities
options.B: Midwives stop keeping records of antenatal clinic attendees
options.C: Maternal deaths are underreported and resource planning is difficult
options.D: Hospitals receive too much funding for emergency blood supplies

explanation: Without accurate data on births and deaths, policymakers cannot target funding or interventions where they are needed most. [learn more](BMP217_U1_T4#BMP217_U1_T4_h5)

question: What is the main focus of quality improvement in maternity care?

options.A: Reducing the total number of hospital admissions
options.B: Waiting for annual external hospital inspections
options.C: Punishing staff who make clinical errors
options.D: Analyzing and improving overall care processes

explanation: Quality improvement looks at underlying systems and processes rather than blaming individuals for mistakes. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T1#BMP217_U2_T1_h1)

question: How does quality improvement differ from traditional quality assurance?

options.A: Quality assurance aims to fix problems permanently on the first attempt.
options.B: Quality improvement is only performed by doctors, while quality assurance is for midwives.
options.C: Quality improvement focuses on continuous system changes rather than just finding individual faults.
options.D: Quality assurance uses data, whereas quality improvement relies purely on personal intuition.

explanation: Traditional inspection looks for who made a mistake, while QI looks at why the system allowed the mistake to happen. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T1#BMP217_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why must maternity care practices never remain static?

options.A: Midwives get easily bored doing the same clinical tasks repeatedly.
options.B: Childbirth can turn life-threatening very quickly and evidence continually evolves.
options.C: International donors will stop funding facilities with old protocols.
options.D: Government policy requires rewriting hospital rulebooks every single month.

explanation: The rapid changes in a patient's condition and new medical findings mean care protocols must constantly adapt. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T1#BMP217_U2_T1_h2)

question: A maternity unit has used the same routine for managing postpartum bleeding for ten years, despite new global guidelines. What is the biggest danger of this approach?

options.A: Midwives will stop charting patient vital signs altogether.
options.B: Mothers may experience preventable complications because care is not updated with current evidence.
options.C: Staff members will lose their nursing licenses immediately.
options.D: The hospital will be closed down by the local health ministry within a week.

explanation: Failing to update practices means patients miss out on safer, modern interventions that could save their lives. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T1#BMP217_U2_T1_h2)

question: Which principle of clinical excellence involves respecting a woman's cultural preferences and choices?

options.A: Patient-centeredness
options.B: Strict standardization
options.C: Cost-efficiency
options.D: Rapid documentation

explanation: Patient-centered care puts the woman, her values, and her dignity at the center of all clinical decisions. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T1#BMP217_U2_T1_h3)

question: What does the principle of timeliness mean in the context of an obstetric emergency like a ruptured uterus?

options.A: Reducing delays in recognizing the problem and providing immediate surgical treatment
options.B: Waiting for the senior consultant to arrive before starting any intravenous line
options.C: Completing the shift handover before attending to the bleeding patient
options.D: Writing down the exact minute the emergency started in the register

explanation: Timeliness is about cutting down crucial minutes between the onset of an emergency and life-saving action. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T1#BMP217_U2_T1_h3)

question: What is the first step in identifying a clinical gap in a maternity unit?

options.A: Comparing current clinical practice against established guidelines
options.B: Ordering new medical equipment from international suppliers
options.C: Punishing staff members who fail to complete patient charts
options.D: Increasing the hospital fees for antenatal booking

explanation: You must compare what is actually happening on the ward against what is supposed to happen according to standards. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T1#BMP217_U2_T1_h4)

question: An audit shows that partograph completion rates in a primary health clinic have dropped to thirty percent. What should the midwife manager do first?

options.A: Report the entire clinic staff to the national medical council.
options.B: Investigate why staff are struggling to complete the partographs during busy hours.
options.C: Fire all the junior midwives working on the night shift.
options.D: Stop using partographs entirely and rely only on clinical intuition.

explanation: Finding the root cause of the gap helps design a practical solution instead of resorting to immediate punishment. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T1#BMP217_U2_T1_h4)

question: During which phase of the PDSA cycle do midwives actually carry out the small-scale clinical test?

options.A: Study phase
options.B: Plan phase
options.C: Act phase
options.D: Do phase

explanation: The 'Do' phase is when the planned intervention is executed on a small scale in the clinical environment. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T1#BMP217_U2_T1_h5)

question: Why is testing changes on a small scale recommended before rolling them out across an entire hospital?

options.A: Government regulations forbid changing hospital rules for more than two wards at once.
options.B: It ensures that patients never notice when new clinical guidelines are introduced.
options.C: Large-scale changes require formal approval from international health organizations.
options.D: It allows the team to find and fix flaws without disrupting the whole facility.

explanation: Small tests minimize risk and let staff see if a new idea works practically before committing the whole hospital to it. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T1#BMP217_U2_T1_h5)

question: What does the communication tool SBAR stand for in clinical handovers?

options.A: Symptoms, Blood pressure, Action, Result
options.B: Safety, Birth, Audit, Review
options.C: Staff, Beds, Apparatus, Records
options.D: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation

explanation: SBAR provides a structured, clear framework for healthcare workers to share critical patient information quickly. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T1#BMP217_U2_T1_h6)

question: Why is establishing a just culture essential for successful quality improvement in a maternity unit?

options.A: It allows hospital management to ignore minor charting errors made by senior doctors.
options.B: It encourages staff to report errors and near-misses honestly without fear of unfair punishment.
options.C: It guarantees that midwives will never make a clinical mistake during night shifts.
options.D: It ensures that patients never sue the hospital for poor obstetric outcomes.

explanation: When people are not afraid of harsh blame, they speak up about system failures, allowing the team to fix them. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T1#BMP217_U2_T1_h6)

question: Which of the following is an example of a process indicator in maternity care?

options.A: The number of babies born with severe congenital abnormalities
options.B: The percentage of mothers who receive oxytocin immediately after delivery
options.C: The overall neonatal mortality rate for the entire hospital
options.D: The total number of maternal deaths recorded in the state over one year

explanation: Process indicators measure whether specific clinical actions and guidelines are actually being carried out by staff. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T1#BMP217_U2_T1_h7)

question: A hospital wants to check if their new training on neonatal resuscitation is changing clinical care. Which data should they track?

options.A: The total amount of money spent on hospital electricity bills
options.B: The total weight of hospital laundry washed each week
options.C: The number of antenatal clinic visits booked during the first trimester
options.D: The proportion of babies requiring resuscitation who are successfully revived within the golden minute

explanation: Tracking resuscitation success directly measures the impact of the training on infant outcomes. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T1#BMP217_U2_T1_h7)

question: What is a common challenge faced when implementing quality improvement in resource-constrained maternity settings?

options.A: Too many administrative staff members in the labor ward
options.B: Erratic power supply and essential drug stockouts
options.C: Excessive funding that is difficult to spend quickly
options.D: An oversupply of highly trained specialist obstetricians

explanation: Clinics often struggle with unreliable utilities and missing supplies, which affect daily service delivery. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T1#BMP217_U2_T1_h8)

question: How can a midwifery team sustain quality improvement when financial resources are very limited?

options.A: By stopping all clinical audits until international grants arrive
options.B: By waiting until the federal government builds a brand new hospital
options.C: By relying on local solutions, peer mentorship, and community-driven support
options.D: By charging patients high private fees for every single routine procedure

explanation: Using local resourcefulness and teamwork helps maintain improvements without needing large financial investments. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T1#BMP217_U2_T1_h8)

question: What is the primary goal of the MPDSR process in a healthcare facility?

options.A: To prevent future maternal and perinatal deaths through systematic review
options.B: To punish healthcare workers who make clinical errors during delivery
options.C: To collect accurate census data for the national government
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of running maternity wards

explanation: MPDSR focuses on understanding why deaths occur so that corrective actions can be put in place to save future lives. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T2#BMP217_U2_T2_h1)

question: Why is MPDSR considered especially important within the Nigerian healthcare context?

options.A: Midwives have extra free time to complete paperwork during night shifts
options.B: International donors require every clinic to submit monthly handwritten reports
options.C: Nigerian hospitals do not record any other types of patient statistics
options.D: Maternal and perinatal mortality ratios remain critically high across the country

explanation: Because Nigeria faces a heavy burden of maternal and newborn deaths, tracking and analyzing these events is essential for saving lives. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T2#BMP217_U2_T2_h1)

question: Within what timeframe should a maternal or perinatal death ideally be notified after it occurs?

options.A: At the end of every quarter
options.B: After exactly one week
options.C: Within 24 hours
options.D: During the annual hospital audit

explanation: Prompt notification within 24 hours ensures that clinical details are fresh and records remain accurate before staff rotate or forget details. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T2#BMP217_U2_T2_h2)

question: A community health extension worker reports that a pregnant woman died at home after prolonged bleeding. How should the facility handle this event under MPDSR?

options.A: Report the family to the local police for failing to seek care
options.B: Ignore it because the patient never reached the hospital gates
options.C: Include it as a community-based maternal death notification for review
options.D: Wait until the end of the year to see if another similar case happens

explanation: MPDSR captures both facility and community deaths to understand delays in seeking and reaching care. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T2#BMP217_U2_T2_h2)

question: When analyzing a maternal death, what does the first delay refer to?

options.A: Delay in writing the final autopsy report
options.B: Delay in deciding to seek medical care
options.C: Delay in transporting the patient to the hospital
options.D: Delay in administering blood in the ward

explanation: The first delay involves the family or patient recognizing danger signs and making the choice to seek help. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T2#BMP217_U2_T2_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of gathering case notes, drug charts, and lab results during an MPDSR audit?

options.A: To provide reading material for incoming midwifery students
options.B: To hide mistakes made by senior doctors from the health ministry
options.C: To calculate the monthly salary bonuses for the maternity unit staff
options.D: To reconstruct an accurate timeline of the clinical events that occurred

explanation: Reviewing all available records helps the audit team see exactly what happened at every stage of the patient's admission. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T2#BMP217_U2_T2_h3)

question: Why must MPDSR audits maintain a strictly blame-free environment?

options.A: To ensure that doctors and midwives never face professional exams
options.B: To encourage honest reporting and prevent staff from hiding clinical errors
options.C: To stop patients from asking questions about their treatment plans
options.D: To allow healthcare workers to ignore hospital Standard Operating Procedures

explanation: When staff know they will not be punished for honest mistakes, they report deaths accurately and discuss system flaws openly. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T2#BMP217_U2_T2_h4)

question: Which of the following practices is essential for protecting patient and staff privacy during an audit?

options.A: Anonymizing names and personal identifiers in review documents
options.B: Publishing the full home addresses of deceased patients in local newspapers
options.C: Recording video footage of the audit meeting to share on social media
options.D: Requiring junior midwives to sign legal confessions for every bad outcome

explanation: Removing names protects patient confidentiality and keeps staff secure from unfair targeting. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T2#BMP217_U2_T2_h4)

question: What does the 'T' stand for in SMART recommendations formulated by an MPDSR committee?

options.A: Total
options.B: Time-bound
options.C: Toxic
options.D: Therapeutic

explanation: SMART stands for Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant, and Time-bound, ensuring deadlines are set for interventions. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T2#BMP217_U2_T2_h5)

question: Which of the following audit recommendations is written correctly according to MPDSR standards?

options.A: Find more money from somewhere to fix the broken roof in the antenatal clinic
options.B: Tell everyone to work harder so that mothers stop dying in our hospital this year
options.C: Procure ten functional delivery couches and train all labor ward staff on postpartum hemorrhage drills within six weeks
options.D: Advise doctors to be more careful whenever they perform a cesarean section

explanation: This recommendation is specific, actionable, and has a clear timeline, unlike vague statements that cannot be measured. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T2#BMP217_U2_T2_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of monitoring implementation after an MPDSR audit?

options.A: To check if the recommendations successfully resolved the identified problems
options.B: To prove to international donors that the hospital has enough computers
options.C: To increase the amount of paperwork required for every maternity admission
options.D: To punish staff members who failed to attend the previous committee meeting

explanation: Monitoring ensures that action plans do not just sit on paper but lead to real changes in patient safety. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T2#BMP217_U2_T2_h6)

question: What helps sustain long-term quality improvement in a maternity unit following routine MPDSR audits?

options.A: Sharing feedback openly and providing continuous supportive supervision to staff
options.B: Keeping all audit committee discussions secret from the regular ward nurses
options.C: Stopping all review meetings once the maternal mortality rate drops slightly
options.D: Relying solely on disciplinary queries whenever a clinical complication arises

explanation: Open communication and supportive supervision keep the team engaged and committed to high standards of care. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T2#BMP217_U2_T2_h6)

question: What is the main goal of clinical governance in healthcare?

options.A: Eliminating the need for written medical records in the ward
options.B: Reducing the monthly salaries of senior nursing staff members
options.C: Continuously improving care quality and safeguarding high standards
options.D: Increasing the number of private patient rooms in the hospital

explanation: Clinical governance provides the structural framework for health facilities to maintain and improve the overall quality of services delivered to patients. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T3#BMP217_U2_T3_h1)

question: Which option is NOT a core pillar of clinical governance in midwifery practice?

options.A: Active involvement of patients and families
options.B: Routine clinical audits of maternity charts
options.C: Strict risk management to protect mothers
options.D: Mandatory private financial investment by staff

explanation: Clinical governance focuses on patient safety, risk reduction, audits, and education, rather than requiring personal financial contributions from healthcare workers. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T3#BMP217_U2_T3_h1)

question: What is the final step in completing a full clinical audit cycle?

options.A: Writing a formal request for government funding
options.B: Destroying all old patient delivery case files
options.C: Firing staff members who failed to follow the protocol
options.D: Conducting a re-audit to measure if care has improved

explanation: After implementing changes, a re-audit is essential to close the loop and verify whether the new interventions successfully improved clinical practice. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T3#BMP217_U2_T3_h2)

question: A maternity ward notices high rates of postpartum hemorrhage and wants to start an audit. What should be their very first step?

options.A: Immediately purchase new brands of intravenous fluids
options.B: Stop all normal vaginal deliveries in the primary health center
options.C: Punish all midwives who recorded high blood loss last month
options.D: Define the best practice standard for managing the third stage of labor

explanation: Before collecting data or making changes, an audit must begin by establishing clear, evidence-based standards of care against which practice will be measured. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T3#BMP217_U2_T3_h2)

question: What primary source should form the foundation of a newly written midwifery clinical protocol?

options.A: Personal opinions of the most senior nurse on duty
options.B: Unverified stories shared on social media platforms
options.C: Old practice manuals from several decades ago
options.D: Reliable research evidence and national health guidelines

explanation: Evidence-based protocols must draw from established research and authorized clinical guidelines to ensure patient safety and care quality. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T3#BMP217_U2_T3_h3)

question: Why is it important for a midwifery protocol to fit the local resource setting?

options.A: To ensure the steps are practical and realistic for the available equipment
options.B: To make sure foreign staff can easily ignore local health needs
options.C: To reduce the total number of pregnant women attending antenatal care
options.D: To bypass the need for any form of clinical audit or monitoring

explanation: Protocols must account for available drugs, staff strength, and equipment in the facility so that midwives can actually follow them in daily practice. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T3#BMP217_U2_T3_h3)

question: Which type of clinical indicator measures the final health result of the mother or baby?

options.A: Financial indicator
options.B: Structure indicator
options.C: Process indicator
options.D: Outcome indicator

explanation: Outcome indicators look at the ultimate result of care, such as recovery rates, complications, or survival statistics. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T3#BMP217_U2_T3_h4)

question: Checking whether every woman in labor had her fetal heart rate monitored every thirty minutes is an example of which indicator type?

options.A: Outcome indicator
options.B: Structure indicator
options.C: Aesthetic indicator
options.D: Process indicator

explanation: Monitoring actions and clinical procedures performed during care delivery fall under process indicators. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T3#BMP217_U2_T3_h4)

question: What does a retrospective chart review involve in a clinical audit?

options.A: Interviewing pregnant women currently sitting in the antenatal waiting hall
options.B: Observing a midwife conduct a live vaginal delivery in the labor room
options.C: Examining already completed patient case files and registers from the past
options.D: Checking the expiry dates of drugs inside the pharmacy storeroom

explanation: Retrospective reviews look backward by analyzing past medical records and delivery registers to assess previous clinical care. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T3#BMP217_U2_T3_h5)

question: Why can poor documentation in delivery registers negatively affect the results of a clinical audit?

options.A: Unrecorded actions are treated as if the care was never provided
options.B: It automatically increases the financial budget of the maternity unit
options.C: It forces the hospital to buy brand new delivery couches
options.D: It prevents patients from ever returning to the antenatal clinic

explanation: Auditors rely entirely on written records; if a procedure is omitted from the notes, it cannot be verified and counts against compliance rates. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T3#BMP217_U2_T3_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of comparing audit data against a benchmark standard?

options.A: To calculate the monthly tax deductions for hospital employees
options.B: To measure the gap between current practice and expected quality
options.C: To test the physical strength of the delivery room furniture
options.D: To determine how many patients were admitted with malaria

explanation: Comparing findings against benchmarks shows precisely where clinical care meets expectations and where performance falls short. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T3#BMP217_U2_T3_h6)

question: Why is it important to investigate the root cause behind a poor audit finding?

options.A: To ensure the corrective intervention targets the real problem
options.B: To delay implementing any changes on the maternity ward
options.C: To find a junior staff member to blame for the failure
options.D: To increase the paperwork required for the next audit cycle

explanation: Understanding why a standard was missed prevents wasting time on solutions that do not address the true underlying barrier. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T3#BMP217_U2_T3_h6)

question: What does the phrase 'closing the audit loop' mean in quality improvement?

options.A: Shutting down the maternity ward for thorough cleaning
options.B: Stopping all clinical meetings until the end of the year
options.C: Conducting a re-audit to check if changes successfully improved care
options.D: Destroying old audit data so no one else can read it

explanation: The loop is closed when you implement changes and return to measure practice again, confirming whether quality actually improved. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T3#BMP217_U2_T3_h7)

question: A maternity unit implemented staff training after an audit showed poor partograph use. What should they do next in the audit process?

options.A: Punish any midwife who still struggles to plot the fetal heart rate
options.B: Wait a few months and perform a re-audit to assess partograph compliance
options.C: Transfer all the trained midwives to the pediatric outpatient department
options.D: Assume the problem is solved forever and never check records again

explanation: Following up with a re-audit after an intervention is the only way to verify if the training actually changed daily clinical habits. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T3#BMP217_U2_T3_h7)

question: What is the primary goal of quality assurance in a maternity delivery unit?

options.A: To reduce the number of staff on duty
options.B: To punish midwives who make clinical mistakes
options.C: To ensure every woman receives safe and respectful care
options.D: To increase the cost of maternity services

explanation: Quality assurance focuses on systematic checks to protect mothers and babies by promoting safe practices rather than punishing staff. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T4#BMP217_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why are frontline midwives considered central to the quality assurance process?

options.A: They write all the national health policies
options.B: They handle only administrative paperwork
options.C: They control the hospital budget and procurement
options.D: They manage normal births and spot early complications

explanation: Midwives interact directly with laboring women, placing them in the best position to deliver care and catch warning signs early. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T4#BMP217_U2_T4_h1)

question: What does a low five-minute Apgar score primarily help midwives evaluate?

options.A: The exact birth weight of the baby
options.B: The effectiveness of intrapartum care and newborn resuscitation
options.C: The mother's blood type and Rhesus factor
options.D: The length of the first stage of labor

explanation: The Apgar score checks how well the baby tolerated the birth process and responded to any help given right after delivery. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T4#BMP217_U2_T4_h2)

question: An unusually high rate of uterine rupture is recorded in a rural hospital delivery unit. What issue does this safety indicator point toward?

options.A: A high number of elective Caesarean sections
options.B: Effective infection control procedures in the theater
options.C: Possible delays in managing obstructed labor or oxytocin misuse
options.D: Excellent routine postnatal counseling for breastfeeding

explanation: Uterine rupture is strongly linked to unmonitored prolonged labor or improper use of drugs that stimulate uterine contractions. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T4#BMP217_U2_T4_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard method for gathering feedback on maternal experience?

options.A: Anonymous suggestion boxes in the postnatal ward
options.B: Secretly reading personal diaries left behind
options.C: Structured questionnaires during immunization visits
options.D: Exit interviews conducted by neutral third parties

explanation: Patient feedback must be gathered through ethical, structured means like interviews and surveys, never by violating personal privacy. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T4#BMP217_U2_T4_h3)

question: Why is it often recommended that neutral third parties conduct exit interviews for new mothers?

options.A: Midwives do not have time to speak any local languages
options.B: Mothers may feel safer to speak honestly without fear of staff backlash
options.C: Hospital management does not care about patient opinions
options.D: Third parties are the only ones who understand medical records

explanation: Patients often fear poor treatment if they criticize the same nurses and midwives who cared for them, so neutral interviewers encourage honest answers. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T4#BMP217_U2_T4_h3)

question: What is the main question a clinical audit tries to answer in a delivery unit?

options.A: What new medical equipment can we buy from abroad?
options.B: Which midwife delivered the highest number of babies?
options.C: Are we actually doing what we know is best practice?
options.D: How much profit did the maternity ward generate this month?

explanation: Clinical audits check current actions against set standards to see where care falls short of guidelines. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T4#BMP217_U2_T4_h4)

question: What is the final step in a standard clinical audit cycle after implementing changes?

options.A: Destroying all records to maintain patient privacy
options.B: Closing the maternity unit for routine fumigation
options.C: Punishing staff members who failed the first review
options.D: Re-auditing to check if clinical practice has improved

explanation: The audit cycle is only complete when you measure again to see if your interventions fixed the problem. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T4#BMP217_U2_T4_h4)

question: What makes a quality improvement strategy effective after reviewing poor hemorrhage data?

options.A: Warning patients not to bleed too much after delivery
options.B: Fines for midwives who forget to chart the time of birth
options.C: Making practical changes like ready-to-use drug packs and staff drills
options.D: Hiding the data so the hospital reputation remains protected

explanation: Effective improvements fix the system workflow rather than just telling workers to try harder. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T4#BMP217_U2_T4_h5)

question: A maternity unit notices patients frequently complain about rude communication from night-shift staff. What is the most appropriate initial quality improvement response?

options.A: Fire all the night-shift midwives immediately without investigation
options.B: Lock the delivery unit doors so patients cannot leave feedback
options.C: Ignore the complaints because night shifts are naturally stressful
options.D: Organize supportive communication workshops and review shift handover routines

explanation: Addressing behavioral issues requires supportive training and looking at systemic factors like fatigue and shift stress. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T4#BMP217_U2_T4_h5)

question: What main sign tells you a pregnant woman with pre-eclampsia has developed eclampsia?

options.A: A sudden spike in maternal body temperature
options.B: Severe vaginal bleeding resembling a placental abruption
options.C: The onset of generalized tonic-clonic seizures
options.D: The complete cessation of fetal heart activity

explanation: Eclampsia is diagnosed when a patient with pre-eclampsia experiences generalized seizures that do not have another neurological cause. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T1#BMP226_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why are changes in vision and bad headaches serious warning signs in a pre-eclamptic patient?

options.A: They indicate severe cerebral vasospasm and impending eclamptic seizures
options.B: They are harmless side effects of routine iron supplementation
options.C: They confirm that the amniotic sac has ruptured prematurely
options.D: They show that the liver is failing to process normal blood proteins

explanation: Headaches and vision changes happen when blood vessels in the brain spasm, signaling that a seizure might be coming. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T1#BMP226_U1_T1_h1)

question: What is the main reason for putting a seizing eclamptic patient on her side?

options.A: To prevent aspiration of vomit and maintain a clear airway
options.B: To completely stop the seizure activity without using drugs
options.C: To speed up the natural descent of the baby's head
options.D: To make it easier to start an intravenous line in the foot

explanation: The side-lying position uses gravity to keep saliva and vomit away from the windpipe, protecting the patient's breathing. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T1#BMP226_U1_T1_h2)

question: What is the first thing a midwife should do when a pregnant woman starts having a seizure in the ward?

options.A: Inject 20mls of sterile water directly into the umbilical cord
options.B: Turn her onto her side and call urgently for emergency assistance
options.C: Perform an immediate vaginal examination to check cervical dilation
options.D: Force a wooden spatula firmly between her teeth to stop tongue biting

explanation: Keeping the airway safe and getting help right away are the critical first steps during a seizure. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T1#BMP226_U1_T1_h2)

question: Which medication is used to reverse magnesium sulfate toxicity?

options.A: Calcium gluconate
options.B: Oxytocin infusion
options.C: Nifedipine tablets
options.D: Atropine sulfate

explanation: Calcium gluconate counteracts too much magnesium in the body and helps restore normal breathing. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T1#BMP226_U1_T1_h3)

question: Why must very high blood pressure in eclampsia be lowered gradually instead of all at once?

options.A: Sudden changes cause the mother's hair to fall out in large clumps
options.B: Normal blood pressure values deactivate the action of magnesium sulfate completely
options.C: Abrupt drops in blood pressure can severely reduce blood flow to the placenta and starve the fetus of oxygen
options.D: Rapid lowering triggers sudden blindness in the postpartum period

explanation: If blood pressure drops too fast, the placenta doesn't get enough blood, which can distress the baby. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T1#BMP226_U1_T1_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT a standard first-choice drug for treating severe high blood pressure in pregnancy?

options.A: Furosemide
options.B: Labetalol
options.C: Nifedipine
options.D: Hydralazine

explanation: Furosemide is a water pill used for fluid in the lungs, not as the primary medicine to bring down dangerously high blood pressure in pregnancy. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T1#BMP226_U1_T1_h4)

question: What is the only treatment that completely cures eclampsia?

options.A: Strict bed rest in a dark room for seven days
options.B: Delivery of the fetus and placenta
options.C: Immediate closure of the cervical os with sutures
options.D: Administration of high-dose intravenous iron

explanation: Eclampsia is caused by the placenta, so delivering it is the only way to stop the underlying condition. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T1#BMP226_U1_T1_h5)

question: When should delivery be planned after a patient has an eclamptic seizure?

options.A: Only after waiting exactly forty-eight hours to ensure lung maturity
options.B: Immediately during the active seizure phase without stopping to stabilize
options.C: Delayed until the patient reaches thirty-seven completed weeks
options.D: Promptly, as soon as maternal stabilization is successfully achieved

explanation: As soon as the mother is stable and safe, delivery should go ahead to protect both her and the baby. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T1#BMP226_U1_T1_h5)

question: How long should magnesium sulfate treatment usually continue after an eclamptic patient gives birth?

options.A: Until breast milk production is established
options.B: For 24 hours post-delivery
options.C: Until the mother is discharged home
options.D: For exactly 2 hours after clamping the cord

explanation: Magnesium sulfate is typically continued for 24 hours after birth to prevent seizures from returning. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T1#BMP226_U1_T1_h6)

question: Why is careful fluid monitoring so important in the postpartum care of a woman with eclampsia?

options.A: To ensure the baby receives enough breast milk every hour
options.B: To prevent fluid overload and subsequent pulmonary edema
options.C: To calculate the exact caloric intake needed for wound healing
options.D: To measure how fast the uterine involution process is occurring

explanation: Kidney changes in eclampsia make it easy for fluid to build up in the lungs if intravenous fluids are given too quickly. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T1#BMP226_U1_T1_h6)

question: What is the name of the ring that forms between the upper and lower parts of the uterus during obstructed labor?

options.A: Schroeder's ring
options.B: Bandl's ring
options.C: Molding ring
options.D: Contraction ring

explanation: Bandl's ring forms when the upper uterine segment thickens and pulls upward while the lower segment stretches thin. It serves as a classic warning sign of an impending uterine rupture. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T2#BMP226_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why does an unscarred uterus sometimes rupture during obstructed labor?

options.A: Extreme stretching of the lower uterine segment due to a blocked delivery
options.B: Rapid descent of the fetal head tearing through a normal cervix
options.C: Sudden softening of the muscle caused by hormone imbalances
options.D: Immediate failure of the placental attachment site under high pressure

explanation: An unscarred uterus can rupture when a physical barrier blocks the baby from descending. This causes the lower uterine segment to stretch excessively until the muscle fibers tear. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T2#BMP226_U1_T2_h1)

question: What is the single greatest risk factor for a uterine rupture in clinical practice?

options.A: Advanced maternal age over forty
options.B: Chronic high blood pressure
options.C: A previous uterine scar from surgery
options.D: A history of multiple miscarriages

explanation: Prior uterine surgery, such as a previous caesarean section, creates an area of structural weakness that is much more likely to tear under the stress of labor. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T2#BMP226_U1_T2_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical factor contributing to uterine rupture in emergency admissions in Nigeria?

options.A: A planned, scheduled repeat caesarean section at term
options.B: Extreme uterine overdistension from carrying many babies
options.C: Inappropriate use of oxytocin by traditional birth attendants
options.D: Neglected obstructed labor from a pelvis that is too small for the baby

explanation: Elective repeat caesarean sections are planned hospital procedures designed to prevent rupture, unlike unmonitored labor or unskilled interventions. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T2#BMP226_U1_T2_h2)

question: What happens to labor contractions immediately after a complete uterine rupture occurs?

options.A: They stay exactly the same
options.B: They become completely painless
options.C: They become much stronger
options.D: They stop completely

explanation: When the uterine muscle tears completely apart, it loses its ability to contract, causing labor pains to cease abruptly. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T2#BMP226_U1_T2_h3)

question: A woman in prolonged labor suddenly screams with sharp belly pain, her contractions stop, and you can feel the baby's parts very clearly right under her skin. What is the most likely diagnosis?

options.A: Impending uterine rupture
options.B: Severe placental abruption
options.C: Normal transition to the second stage of labor
options.D: Complete uterine rupture

explanation: The sudden stopping of contractions, sharp tearing pain, and easy feeling of baby parts outside the uterus point directly to a complete rupture. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T2#BMP226_U1_T2_h3)

question: Why might vaginal bleeding seem surprisingly small in a patient with a complete uterine rupture?

options.A: The baby's body blocks the blood from leaking outward
options.B: The cervix remains tightly closed and traps all blood inside
options.C: Most of the bleeding goes directly into the abdominal cavity
options.D: Uterine contractions squeeze the blood vessels shut

explanation: Because the wall of the uterus is torn open, the bleeding escapes into the mother's abdominal cavity rather than flowing down through the vagina. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T2#BMP226_U1_T2_h4)

question: What is one of the earliest signs that the baby is in severe trouble after a uterine rupture?

options.A: Prolonged early decelerations during contractions
options.B: Passing meconium early while still preterm
options.C: Severe fetal distress followed by absent heart sounds
options.D: A sudden rise in the baseline fetal heart rate

explanation: When the uterus tears and blood flow is lost, the baby is quickly cut off from oxygen, leading to severe distress and absent heart sounds. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T2#BMP226_U1_T2_h4)

question: Which treatment must be strictly avoided when first caring for a patient with a suspected uterine rupture?

options.A: Inserting a urinary catheter
options.B: Giving an oxytocin infusion
options.C: Setting up large IV lines for fluids
options.D: Monitoring urine output hourly

explanation: Giving oxytocin makes the damaged uterus contract forcefully, which can widen the tear and dangerously increase internal bleeding. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T2#BMP226_U1_T2_h5)

question: Why is a urinary catheter placed immediately when treating a patient with a ruptured uterus?

options.A: To drain fluid directly out of the abdominal cavity
options.B: To collect clean urine samples to check for infections
options.C: To monitor kidney function and blood flow through hourly urine output
options.D: To keep the bladder from filling up and blocking future surgery

explanation: Tracking urine output is a reliable way to check if fluid replacement is successfully restoring blood flow to vital organs after heavy bleeding. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T2#BMP226_U1_T2_h5)

question: What is the main surgery performed to treat a complete uterine rupture?

options.A: Transcervical resection
options.B: Emergency laparotomy
options.C: Diagnostic laparoscopy
options.D: Manual vacuum aspiration

explanation: An open surgical exploration of the abdomen, called a laparotomy, is necessary to view the tear, stop the bleeding, and safely deliver the baby. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T2#BMP226_U1_T2_h6)

question: When would a surgeon choose to remove the uterus (hysterectomy) instead of repairing it after a rupture?

options.A: When the tear is very large, ragged, or the mother's life is in immediate danger
options.B: When the tear is small and only affects the lower scar
options.C: When the patient is having her first baby and wants more children
options.D: When there is no active bleeding inside the abdomen

explanation: Severe, ragged tears or uncontrolled bleeding make repairing the uterus unsafe. A hysterectomy is then done to stop the bleeding and save the mother's life. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T2#BMP226_U1_T2_h6)

question: What is the primary reason why babies sadly have a very high mortality rate during a uterine rupture?

options.A: Severe maternal dehydration before getting to the hospital
options.B: Sudden lack of oxygen because the placenta separates
options.C: Genetic birth defects in the baby
options.D: Direct injury from surgical tools

explanation: When the uterus tears and the placenta pulls away, the baby is instantly cut off from its oxygen supply, leading to rapid suffocation. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T2#BMP226_U1_T2_h7)

question: Which complication often happens along with a severe uterine tear that spreads to the sides?

options.A: Severe high blood sugar in the mother
options.B: Damage to the ureters or bladder
options.C: Rupture of the mother's spleen
options.D: Damage to the abdominal wall muscles

explanation: Because the lower uterus sits right next to the urinary tract, tears that spread to the sides put the bladder and ureters at high risk of accidental injury. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T2#BMP226_U1_T2_h7)

question: Why are patients encouraged to walk around early during recovery after a laparotomy?

options.A: To help start breast milk production
options.B: To make the skin incision heal faster
options.C: To prevent dangerous blood clots in the veins
options.D: To help the uterus shrink back to normal size

explanation: Getting patients up and moving early improves blood flow in the legs, which greatly lowers the risk of harmful blood clots forming. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T2#BMP226_U1_T2_h8)

question: A patient who had her uterus repaired after a rupture is ready to go home. What key advice should the midwife emphasize?

options.A: Try to get pregnant within six months to keep the scar soft
options.B: Avoid all physical activity to protect the belly muscles
options.C: Plan for a home birth with a traditional birth attendant next time
options.D: Use family planning strictly and book early for antenatal care in future pregnancies

explanation: A repaired uterus has a high chance of rupturing again in a future pregnancy. Reliable birth control and early, supervised hospital care are essential for her safety. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T2#BMP226_U1_T2_h8)

question: By what percentage does a pregnant woman's blood volume usually increase?

options.A: Roughly seventy percent
options.B: Up to forty percent
options.C: Around ten percent
options.D: Exactly five percent

explanation: Pregnancy causes blood volume to increase by up to forty percent to help support the growing baby and placenta. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T3#BMP226_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why might a pregnant woman bleed a lot without showing an immediate drop in blood pressure?

options.A: Hormones during pregnancy permanently block low blood pressure
options.B: The placenta stores extra blood to maintain high systemic pressure
options.C: Her body compensates through vasoconstriction and increased heart rate
options.D: Fetal blood circulation directly supports maternal blood pressure

explanation: Early blood loss triggers a faster heart rate and tightening of blood vessels, which hides the drop in blood pressure until those mechanisms fail. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T3#BMP226_U1_T3_h1)

question: What is the most common cause of hypovolemic shock in pregnancy and childbirth?

options.A: Severe pelvic infection
options.B: Peripartum cardiomyopathy
options.C: Postpartum hemorrhage
options.D: Amniotic fluid embolism

explanation: Heavy bleeding after childbirth is the leading cause of hypovolemic shock in women during the postpartum period. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T3#BMP226_U1_T3_h2)

question: Which type of shock is mainly caused by a severe body-wide infection and widespread blood vessel widening?

options.A: Septic shock
options.B: Obstructive shock
options.C: Cardiogenic shock
options.D: Hypovolemic shock

explanation: Infection releases chemicals in the body that cause blood vessels to widen massively, leading to septic shock. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T3#BMP226_U1_T3_h2)

question: What is usually the earliest warning sign of hypovolemic shock in a pregnant patient?

options.A: Hypotension
options.B: Hypertension
options.C: Bradycardia
options.D: Tachycardia

explanation: An increased heart rate happens early as the body tries to keep blood moving despite a drop in total volume. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T3#BMP226_U1_T3_h3)

question: A postpartum woman has normal blood pressure but feels anxious, has cold skin, and a fast pulse. What should the midwife suspect?

options.A: A mild panic attack unrelated to blood loss
options.B: Normal physiological recovery after delivery
options.C: Fluid overload from intravenous infusions
options.D: Compensated shock requiring urgent investigation

explanation: Normal blood pressure can hide early shock when the body is working hard to compensate, making other physical signs very important to notice. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T3#BMP226_U1_T3_h3)

question: What size of intravenous line is preferred when managing a patient in severe obstetric shock?

options.A: Central lines exclusively
options.B: Large-bore cannulas
options.C: Midline pediatric lines
options.D: Small butterfly needles

explanation: Large-bore IV lines are needed to quickly give fluids and blood products during major bleeding emergencies. [learn more](BMP226_U1_T3#BMP226_U1_T3_h4)

question: Why is giving too much plain IV fluid discouraged during uncontrolled bleeding?

options.A: It stops the heart from beating effectively
options.B: It dilutes existing clotting factors and worsens bleeding
